title: A Relationship Between Nonphysical Quasi-probabilities and Nonlocality Objectivity

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The listed quantities cannot be the eigenvalues of rho as defined in Eq. (1). Each of the four values in Eq. (6) has baseline 1, so their sum is 2(1+c_p)+2(1-c_p)=4, whereas Tr(rho)=1. The formulas require an overall factor 1/4. The same missing factor persists in Eq. (7). Consequently, statements that identify a geometric distance directly with the minimum eigenvalue, including the construction of an eigenvalue lambda_0 in Theorem 1.4, are numerically wrong by a factor of four.

predicted_errors.error_location: Eq. (8) and the derivation of Eq. (9)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Eq. (8) does not correctly compute beta^T beta. beta^T beta must be a 3-by-3 matrix, but the displayed objects are 3-by-1 column vectors. More importantly, if beta has one nonzero row r=(beta_1,beta_2,beta_3), then beta^T beta=r^T r, with eigenvalues ||r||^2,0,0, not the separate squared entries beta_1^2,beta_2^2,beta_3^2. If beta has one nonzero column c, then beta^T beta has one diagonal entry ||c||^2 and two zero entries. In both cases the Horodecki quantity is ||beta||^2, not beta_1^2+beta_2^2 in one orientation and beta_1^2+beta_2^2+beta_3^2 in the other. Thus Eq. (9) does not provide conditions for a SIN state.

A qubit swap sends the correlation matrix beta to beta^T. beta and beta^T have exactly the same singular values, so beta^T beta and beta beta^T have the same eigenvalues. Therefore the Horodecki CHSH quantity M, the sum of the two largest squared singular values, is invariant under the swap for every two-qubit operator, not merely physical states. A state cannot be CHSH-nonlocal before swapping and CHSH-local after swapping. This directly disproves the claimed swap-intolerant nonlocal construction and the main theorem.

The manuscript applies the Horodecki theorem to explicitly non-positive-semidefinite operators and calls the resulting classifications 'local' and 'nonlocal.' The theorem is a criterion for CHSH violation by a physical two-qubit density operator: positivity is required so that measurement outcomes define probabilities and correlations. A Hermitian trace-one operator with negative eigenvalues is not a quantum state and does not furnish operational Bell probabilities. At most, the algebraic expression M can be evaluated; it cannot establish observer-dependent physical nonlocality or a connection to 'nonlocal objectivism.'

predicted_errors.error_location: Final conclusion beginning 'Furthermore, the boundary for nonlocality...'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The claimed identification of the positive-semidefinite boundary with the nonlocality boundary is unsupported and false. Even in the manuscript's own sphere description, positive semidefiniteness depends on C and the radii r_+ and r_-, whereas the proposed CHSH threshold is |E|=1 and depends only on beta. Proposition 3.1 only supplies a necessary restriction for positive states in this subclass; it does not make |E|=1 the full positivity boundary. More generally, positivity and the CHSH-violation boundary are distinct conditions.

Eq. (1) is presented as a general trace-one two-qubit density-matrix expansion while stating that the indices refer to Pauli operators labelled X,Y,Z,I. If the displayed double sum includes i=j=I, as written, it adds c_II I_4 to the separately written I_4 term, and Tr(rho)=1+c_II rather than 1. The formula must explicitly exclude (i,j)=(I,I), or explicitly state c_II=0. Without that restriction, it is inconsistent with Eq. (2) and is not the claimed normalized general representation.

predicted_errors.error_location: References and all citations [1]-[7], especially the reliance on [4]
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper cites [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6], and [7] throughout, including attribution of the central eigenvalue formula and Proposition 2.1 to [4], but the supplied bibliography contains only reference [8]. The cited Bell, Horodecki, hyperplane-state, and doily sources are therefore unidentified and unverifiable. In particular, the central external result purportedly supplying Eq. predicted_errors.error_location: All embedded figures and their references
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The prose refers to Fig. 1, Fig. 2, and Fig. 3, but the document embeds six unlabeled images numbered Figure 0 through Figure 5, with no captions identifying their contents. Figure 5 is inserted in the middle of the concluding sentence ('It is the boundary that defines' ... figure ... '|E| = 1'). Figures 0, 4, and 5 are never cited, and the numbering does not unambiguously match the cited figures. This prevents verification of the geometric assertions said to be illustrated by the figures and indicates a corrupted or incorrectly assembled manuscript.
